newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end firm on late fund buying rally.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end firm on late fund buying rally.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed higher on a late spate of fund and commercial buying after struggling most of the session with bearish weather reports from key South American growing regions, traders said.
"We've had enormous gains of late and the bears have been trying to break the market but with very little success," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.

Traders said Cargill Inc and Iowa Grain each bought 500,000 bushels March in late dealings which helped turn the market around. Refco Inc and Merrill Lynch were also major buyers on the close, traders said.

Merrill Lynch bought at least six million bushels March on the day while Refco Inc bought at least five million bushels in late dealings after selling four million bushels earlier in the session, traders said.
Traders said a private 1997-98 U.S. corn and soybean acreage estimate was due Friday. Some of the late buying was tied to position squaring ahead of that estimate, they said.
Soybeans closed 1/4 to 3-1/4 cents per bushel higher with March up 2-3/4 at $7.48-1/4. The March contract has gained nearly 50 cents per bushel since last Thursday.

Meteorologists continued to send conflicting messages about expected weekend rains in parched Brazilian soybean areas. Some said showers would be widespread while others suggested they would be more scattered.

USDA's weekly export data was considered supportive for soybeans. USDA said U.S. net exports of soybeans for the week ended January 9 totaled 712,500 tonnes, near the high end of expectations for 500,000 to 800,000 tonnes.
